verses.text: For di ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, for di tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all im army come against Jerusalem, and dem besiege am.
For di eleventh year of Zedekiah, for di fourth month, di ninth day of di month, dem break through di city.

All di princes of di king of Babylon come in, and sit for di middle gate: Nergal Sharezer, Samgar Nebo, Sarsechim Rabsaris, Nergal Sharezer Rabmag, with all di rest of di princes of di king of Babylon.

E happen, say when Zedekiah king of Judah and all di men of war see dem, den dem flee, and go out of di city by night, by di way of di king garden, through di gate between di two walls. E go out toward di Arabah.

But di army of di Chaldeans pursue dem, and overtake Zedekiah for di plains of Jericho. When dem don take am, dem bring am up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah for di land of Hamath, and e pronounce judgment on am.
Di king of Babylon kill di sons of Zedekiah for Riblah before im eyes. Di king of Babylon kill also all di nobles of Judah.
Moreover e put out Zedekiah eyes, and bind am with bronze fetters, to carry am to Babylon.
Di Chaldeans burn di king house, and di houses of di people, with fire, and break down di walls of Jerusalem.
Den Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard carry away captive to Babylon di remnant of di people wey remain for di city, and di deserters wey fall away to am, and di rest of di people wey remain.
But Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard leave some of di poor of di people, wey get nothing, for di land of Judah, and give dem vineyards and fields at di same time.
Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon give charge concerning Jeremiah by Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard, saying,
“Take am, and look well to am, and do am no harm, but do to am even as e go talk to you.”
So Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard send, and Nebushazban Rabsaris, and Nergal Sharezer Rabmag, and all di chief officers of di king of Babylon,
dem send, and take Jeremiah out of di court of di guard, and commit am to Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, Shaphan pikin, to carry am home. So e dwell among di people.
Now di word of di Lord come to Jeremiah, while e dey shut up for di court of di guard, say,

“Go, and speak to Ebed Melech di Ethiopian, saying, ‘Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: See, I go bring my words on dis city for evil, and no for good. Dem go dey accomplished before you for dat day.
But I go deliver you for dat day,’ talk di Lord. ‘Dem no go give you into di hand of di men of whom you dey afraid.
Because I go surely save you, and you no go fall by di sword, but your life go be to you for plunder, because you don put your trust for me,’ talk di Lord.”

Di word wey come to Jeremiah from di Lord, after Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard don let am go from Ramah, when e take am, bound in chains among all di captives of Jerusalem and Judah, wey dem dey carry away captive to Babylon.
Di captain of di guard take Jeremiah, and talk to am, “Di Lord your God pronounce dis evil on dis place,
and di Lord don bring am, and do according as e don speak, because una don sin against di Lord, and no obey im voice. Therefore dis thing don come on una.

Now see, I loose you today from di chains wey dey your hand. If e seem good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I go look well to you. But if e seem bad to you to come with me to Babylon, no come. See, all di land dey before you. Go wherever e seem good and right to you to go.

While e never go back, go back den to Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, Shaphan pikin, wey di king of Babylon don make governor over di cities of Judah, and dwell with am among di people, or go wherever e seem right to you to go.” So di captain of di guard give am provisions and gift, and let am go.
Den Jeremiah go to Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, to Mizpah, and dwell with am among di people wey remain for di land.

Now when all di captains of di forces wey dey di field, dem and dem men, hear say di king of Babylon don make Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, governor for di land, and don commit to am men, and women, and children, and some of di poorest of di land, of dem wey no dey carried away captive to Babylon,

den dem come to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, and Johanan and Jonathan, Kareah pikin, and Seraiah, Tanhumeth pikin, and di sons of Ephai di Netophathite, and Jezaniah, di son of di Maacathite, dem and dem men.
Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, Shaphan pikin, swear to dem and to dem men, saying, “No fear to serve di Chaldeans. Dwell for di land, and serve di king of Babylon, and e go dey well with you.

As for me, see, I go dwell for Mizpah, to stand before di Chaldeans wey go come to us. But una, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and put dem for una vessels, and dwell for una cities wey una don take.”

Likewise when all di Jews wey dey Moab, and among di children of Ammon, and for Edom, and wey dey all di countries, hear say di king of Babylon don leave remnant to Judah, and say e don set over dem Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, Shaphan pikin,
den all di Jews return out of all di places where dem dey driven, and come to di land of Judah, to Gedaliah, to Mizpah, and gather wine and summer fruits very plenty.
Moreover Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di captains of di forces wey dey di field, come to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
and talk to am, “You know say Baalis di king of di children of Ammon don send Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, to take your life?” But Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, no believe dem.

Den Johanan, Kareah pikin, speak to Gedaliah for Mizpah secretly, saying, “Make I go, I beg you, and I go kill Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, and nobody go know am. Why e go take your life, so that all di Jews wey gather to you go scatter, and di remnant of Judah perish?”
But Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, talk to Johanan, Kareah pikin, “You no go do dis thing, because you speak falsely of Ishmael.”

Now e happen for di seventh month, say Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, Elishama pikin, of di royal offspring, and one of di chief officers of di king, and ten men with am, come to Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, to Mizpah. Dere dem eat bread together for Mizpah.

Den Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, rise up, with di ten men wey dey with am, and strike Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, Shaphan pikin, with di sword, and kill am, wey di king of Babylon don make governor over di land.
Ishmael kill also all di Jews wey dey with am, even with Gedaliah, for Mizpah, and di Chaldeans wey dem find dere, di men of war.
E happen di second day after e don kill Gedaliah, and nobody know am,

say dere come men from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even 80 men, with dem beards shaved, and dem clothes torn, and dem don cut demselves, with offerings and incense for dem hand, to bring dem to di house of di Lord.
Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, go out from Mizpah to meet dem, weeping all as e dey go. E happen, as e meet dem, e talk to dem, “Come to Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin.”
E happen, when dem come into di middle of di city, say Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, kill dem, and cast dem into di middle of di pit, e and di men wey dey with am.
But ten men dey found among dem wey talk to Ishmael, “No kill us, because we get treasures hidden for di field: wheat, barley, oil, and honey.” So e stop, and no kill dem among dem brothers.

Now di pit wey Ishmael cast all di dead bodies of di men wey e don kill, because of Gedaliah, na di one wey Asa di king don make for fear of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, fill am with dem wey dem kill.

Den Ishmael carry away captive all di remnant of di people wey dey Mizpah, di king daughters, and all di people wey remain for Mizpah, wey Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard don commit to Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin. Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, carry dem away captive, and depart to go over to di children of Ammon.
But when Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di captains of di forces wey dey with am, hear all di evil wey Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, don do,
den dem take all di men, and go to fight with Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, and find am by di great waters wey dey Gibeon.
E happen, say when all di people wey dey with Ishmael see Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di captains of di forces wey dey with am, den dem rejoice.
So all di people wey Ishmael don carry away captive from Mizpah turn about and return, and go to Johanan, Kareah pikin.
But Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, escape from Johanan with eight men, and go to di children of Ammon.

Den Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di captains of di forces wey dey with am, take all di remnant of di people, wey e don recover from Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, from Mizpah, after e don kill Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, even di men of war, and di women, and di children, and di eunuchs, wey e don bring again from Gibeon.
Dem go and dwell for Geruth Chimham, wey dey by Bethlehem, to go to enter Egypt,
because of di Chaldeans. Because dem dey afraid of dem, because Ishmael, Nethaniah pikin, don kill Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, wey di king of Babylon make governor over di land.
Den all di captains of di forces, and Johanan, Kareah pikin, and Jezaniah, Hoshaiah pikin, and all di people from di least even to di greatest, come near,

and talk to Jeremiah di prophet, “Make we beg you, make our supplication dey accepted before you, and pray for us to di Lord your God, even for all dis remnant (because we dey left but few out of many, as your eyes see us),
so that di Lord your God go show us di way wey we go waka, and di thing wey we go do.”

Den Jeremiah di prophet talk to dem, “I don hear una. See, I go pray to di Lord una God according to una words. E go happen say whatever di Lord go answer una, I go declare am to una. I go keep nothing back from una.”
Den dem talk to Jeremiah, “Make di Lord be true and faithful witness between us, if we no do even according to all di word wey di Lord your God go send you to us.
Whether e dey good or whether e dey evil, we go obey di voice of di Lord our God, to whom we dey send you, so that e go dey well with us, when we obey di voice of di Lord our God.”
E happen after ten days, say di word of di Lord come to Jeremiah.
Den e call Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di captains of di forces wey dey with am, and all di people from di least even to di greatest,
and talk to dem, “Di Lord, di God of Israel, to whom una send me to present una supplication before am, talk like dis:
If una go still dwell for dis land, den I go build una, and no pull una down, and I go plant una, and no pluck una up, because I relent of di evil wey I don do to una.
No dey afraid of di king of Babylon, of whom una dey afraid. No dey afraid of am,” talk di Lord, “because I dey with una to save una, and to deliver una from im hand.
I go show mercies to una, so that e go have mercy on una, and cause una to return to una own land.”
But if una talk, ‘We no go dwell for dis land,’ so that una no obey di voice of di Lord una God,
saying, ‘No, but we go go into di land of Egypt, where we no go see war, nor hear di sound of di trumpet, nor dey hungry for bread, and dere we go dwell,’
now therefore hear di word of di Lord, remnant of Judah. Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “If una wholly set una faces to enter Egypt, and go to sojourn dere,
den e go happen, say di sword wey una dey afraid of go overtake una dere for di land of Egypt, and di famine wey una dey dread go follow hard after una dere for Egypt, and dere una go die.

So e go be with all di men wey set dem faces to go into Egypt to sojourn dere. Dem go die by di sword, by di famine, and by di pestilence. None of dem go remain or escape from di evil wey I go bring on dem.”

Because di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “As my anger and my wrath don dey poured out on di inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath go dey poured out on una, when una enter Egypt. Una go be curse, and astonishment, and imprecation, and reproach. Una no go see dis place again.”
Di Lord don talk concerning una, remnant of Judah, “No go into Egypt.” Know certainly say I don warn una today.
Because una don deceive una souls, because una send me to di Lord una God, saying, “Pray for us to di Lord our God, and declare to us all wey di Lord our God go talk, and we go do am.”
I don declare am to una today, but una no obey di voice of di Lord una God, in anything for which e don send me to una.
Now therefore know certainly say una go die by di sword, by di famine, and by di pestilence, for di place where una desire to go to sojourn.
E happen, when Jeremiah don finish speaking to all di people all di words of di Lord dem God, wey di Lord dem God don send am to dem, even all dis words,
den Azariah, Hoshaiah pikin, and Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di proud men talk to Jeremiah, “You speak falsely. Di Lord our God no send you to talk, ‘No go into Egypt to sojourn dere,’
but Baruch, Neriah pikin, set you against us, so that e go deliver us into di hand of di Chaldeans, so that dem go put us to death, and carry us away captive to Babylon.”
So Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di captains of di forces, and all di people, no obey di voice of di Lord, to dwell for di land of Judah.
But Johanan, Kareah pikin, and all di captains of di forces, take all di remnant of Judah, wey don return from all di nations where dem dey driven, to sojourn for di land of Judah:

di men, and di women, and di children, and di king daughters, and every person wey Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard don leave with Gedaliah, Ahikam pikin, Shaphan pikin, and Jeremiah di prophet, and Baruch, Neriah pikin.
Dem come into di land of Egypt, because dem no obey di voice of di Lord. Dem come even to Tahpanhes.
Den di word of di Lord come to Jeremiah for Tahpanhes, say,
“Take great stones for your hand, and hide dem for di mortar for di brick pavement wey dey di entry of Pharaoh house for Tahpanhes, for di sight of di men of Judah,

and talk to dem, ‘Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: See, I go send and take Nebuchadnezzar di king of Babylon, my servant, and I go set im throne on dis stones wey I don hide. E go spread im royal canopy over dem.
E go come, and go strike di land of Egypt: dem wey dey for death, to death. Dem wey dey for captivity, to captivity. Dem wey dey for di sword, to di sword.

I go kindle fire for di houses of di gods of Egypt. E go burn dem, and carry dem away captive. E go array imself with di land of Egypt, as shepherd put on im cloak, and e go go out from dere in peace.
E go also break di pillars of Beth Shemesh, wey dey di land of Egypt. E go burn di houses of di gods of Egypt with fire.’”
Di word wey come to Jeremiah concerning all di Jews wey dwell for di land of Egypt, wey dwell for Migdol, and for Tahpanhes, and for Memphis, and for di country of Pathros, say,
“Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: Una don see all di evil wey I don bring on Jerusalem, and on all di cities of Judah. See, dis day dem dey desolation, and no man dwell inside dem,
because of dem wickedness wey dem don commit to provoke me to anger, in that dem go burn incense, and serve other gods wey dem no know, neither dem, nor una, nor una fathers.
Yet I send to una all my servants di prophets, rising early and sending dem, saying, ‘Oh, no do dis abominable thing wey I hate.’
But dem no listen, nor incline dem ear to turn from dem wickedness, to burn no incense to other gods.
Therefore my wrath and my anger dey poured out, and dey kindled for di cities of Judah and for di streets of Jerusalem. Dem dey wasted and desolate, as e dey dis day.

Now therefore di Lord, di God of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: Why una commit dis great evil against una own souls, to cut off from una man and woman, child and infant, out of Judah, to leave una none remaining,

in that una provoke me to anger with di works of una hands, burning incense to other gods for di land of Egypt, where una don go to sojourn, so that una go cut yourselves off, and so that una go be curse and reproach among all di nations of di earth?

Una don forget di wickedness of una fathers, and di wickedness of di kings of Judah, and di wickedness of dem wives, and una own wickedness, and di wickedness of una wives, wey dem commit for di land of Judah and for di streets of Jerusalem?
Dem no dey humbled even to dis day, neither dem fear, nor waka for my law, nor for my statutes, wey I set before una and before una fathers.
Therefore di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: See, I go set my face against una for evil, even to cut off all Judah.

I go take di remnant of Judah, wey don set dem faces to go into di land of Egypt to sojourn dere, and dem all go dey consumed. Dem go fall for di land of Egypt. Dem go dey consumed by di sword and by di famine. Dem go die, from di least even to di greatest, by di sword and by di famine. Dem go be curse, and astonishment, and imprecation, and reproach.
Because I go punish dem wey dwell for di land of Egypt, as I don punish Jerusalem, by di sword, by di famine, and by di pestilence,

so that none of di remnant of Judah, wey don go into di land of Egypt to sojourn dere, go escape or remain, so that dem go return to di land of Judah, to which dem long to return to dwell dere, because none go return except some wey escape.”

Den all di men wey know say dem wives burn incense to other gods, and all di women wey stand by, great assembly, even all di people wey dwell for di land of Egypt, for Pathros, answer Jeremiah, saying,
“As for di word wey you don speak to us for di name of di Lord, we no go listen to you.

But we go surely do whatever go out of our mouth, to burn incense to di queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings to am, as we don do, we and our fathers, our kings and our princes, for di cities of Judah and for di streets of Jerusalem. Because den we get plenty of food, and dey well, and see no evil.
But since we leave off burning incense to di queen of heaven, and pouring out drink offerings to am, we don lack all things, and don dey consumed by di sword and by di famine.”
Di women talk, “When we burn incense to di queen of heaven, and pour out drink offerings to am, we make cakes to am to worship am, and pour out drink offerings to am, without our husbands?”
Den Jeremiah talk to all di people, to di men, and to di women, even to all di people wey answer am, saying,

“Di incense wey una burn for di cities of Judah and for di streets of Jerusalem, una and una fathers, una kings and una princes, and di people of di land, di Lord no remember dem, and e no come into im mind?

So that di Lord no fit bear again, because of di evil of una doings, and because of di abominations wey una don commit. Therefore una land don become desolation, and astonishment, and curse, without inhabitant, as e dey dis day.

Because una don burn incense, and because una don sin against di Lord, and no obey di voice of di Lord, nor waka for im law, nor for im statutes, nor for im testimonies, therefore dis evil don happen to una, as e dey dis day.”
Moreover Jeremiah talk to all di people, and to all di women, “Hear di word of di Lord, all Judah wey dey di land of Egypt.”

“Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: ‘Una and una wives don both speak with una mouths, and fulfil with una hand, saying, “We go surely perform our vows wey we don vow, to burn incense to di queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings to am.” Go ahead then, establish una vows, and perform una vows.’

Therefore hear di word of di Lord, all Judah wey dwell for di land of Egypt: ‘See, I don swear by my great name,’ talk di Lord, ‘say my name no go dey named again for di mouth of any man of Judah for all di land of Egypt, saying, “As di Lord God live.”
See, I dey watch over dem for evil, and no for good. All di men of Judah wey dey di land of Egypt go dey consumed by di sword and by di famine, until dem dey consumed.

Dem wey escape di sword go return out of di land of Egypt into di land of Judah, few in number. All di remnant of Judah, wey don go into di land of Egypt to sojourn dere, go know whose word go stand, mine or dem own.
Dis go be di sign to una,’ talk di Lord, ‘say I go punish una for dis place, so that una go know say my words go surely stand against una for evil.

Di Lord talk like dis: See, I go give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into di hand of im enemies, and into di hand of dem wey seek im life, as I give Zedekiah king of Judah into di hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, im enemy, wey seek im life.’”
Di word wey Jeremiah di prophet speak to Baruch, Neriah pikin, when e write dis words for scroll from di mouth of Jeremiah, for di fourth year of Jehoiakim, Josiah pikin, king of Judah, say,
“Di Lord, di God of Israel, talk like dis to you, Baruch:
You talk, ‘Woe to me now! Because di Lord don add sorrow to my pain. I dey weary with my groaning, and I no find rest.’
Talk to am like dis: ‘Di Lord talk like dis: See, wetin I don build, I go break down, and wetin I don plant, I go pluck up, even all dis land.
You dey seek great things for yourself? No seek dem, because see, I go bring evil on all flesh,’ talk di Lord, ‘but I go give your life to you for plunder for all di places where you go.’”
Di word of di Lord wey come to Jeremiah di prophet against di nations.

Concerning Egypt: against di army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, wey dey by di river Euphrates for Carchemish, wey Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon strike for di fourth year of Jehoiakim, Josiah pikin, king of Judah.
“Prepare buckler and shield, and draw near to battle!
Harness di horses, and get up, una horsemen, and stand forth with una helmets. Polish di spears. Put on di coats of mail.
Why I don see am? Dem dey dismayed and turn backward. Dem mighty ones dey beaten down, and flee in haste. Dem no look back. Terror dey on every side,” talk di Lord.
“No make di swift flee away, nor di mighty man escape. For di north by di river Euphrates dem don stumble and fall.
Who be dis wey rise up like di Nile, whose waters toss like di rivers?
Egypt rise up like di Nile, and im waters toss like di rivers. E talk, ‘I go rise up. I go cover di earth. I go destroy city and di inhabitants of am.’
Go up, una horses! Rage, una chariots! Make di mighty men go forth: Cush and Put, wey handle di shield, and di Ludim, wey handle and bend di bow.

Dat day na di day of di Lord, di Lord of Armies, day of vengeance, so that e go avenge imself of im adversaries. Di sword go devour and be satisfied, and drink im fill of dem blood, because di Lord, di Lord of Armies, get sacrifice for di north country by di river Euphrates.
Go up into Gilead, and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. For vain you multiply medicines. No healing dey for you.
Di nations don hear of your shame, and your cry fill di earth, because di mighty man don stumble against di mighty man. Dem two don fall together.”
Di word wey di Lord speak to Jeremiah di prophet, how Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon go come and strike di land of Egypt:
“Declare am for Egypt, and publish for Migdol, and publish for Memphis and for Tahpanhes. Talk, ‘Stand firm, and prepare yourself, because di sword don devour round about you.’
Why your strong ones dey swept away? Dem no stand, because di Lord drive dem.
E make many to stumble. Yes, dem fall one upon another. Dem talk, ‘Arise! Make we go again to our own people, and to di land of our birth, from di oppressing sword.’
Dem cry dere, ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt na only noise. E don let di appointed time pass by.’
As I live,” talk di King, wey im name na di Lord of Armies, “surely like Tabor among di mountains, and like Carmel by di sea, so e go come.
You daughter wey dwell for Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity, because Memphis go become desolation, and go dey burned up, without inhabitant.
Egypt na very beautiful heifer, but destruction don come from di north. E don come.

Also her hired men inside her dey like fattened calves, because dem also don turn back. Dem don flee away together. Dem no stand, because di day of dem calamity don come on dem, di time of dem visitation.
Her sound go go like serpent, because dem go march with army, and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.
Dem go cut down her forest,” talk di Lord, “though e no fit dey searched, because dem pass di locusts, and dem no fit dey counted.
Di daughter of Egypt go dey disgraced. E go dey delivered into di hand of di people of di north.”
Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk, “See, I go punish Amon of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with her gods and her kings, even Pharaoh, and dem wey trust for am.

I go deliver dem into di hand of dem wey seek dem life, and into di hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into di hand of im servants. Afterward e go dey inhabited, as for di days of old,” talk di Lord.

“But no fear, my servant Jacob, neither dey dismayed, Israel, because see, I go save you from far, and your offspring from di land of dem captivity. Jacob go return, and go dey quiet and at ease, and none go make am afraid.

No fear, Jacob my servant,” talk di Lord, “because I dey with you. Because I go make full end of all di nations where I don drive you, but I no go make full end of you, but I go correct you in measure, and I no go leave you altogether unpunished.”
Di word of di Lord wey come to Jeremiah di prophet against di Philistines, before Pharaoh strike Gaza.

Di Lord talk like dis: “See, waters rise up out of di north, and go become overflowing stream, and go overflow di land and all wey dey inside am, di city and dem wey dwell inside am. Di men go cry, and all di inhabitants of di land go howl.
At di noise of di stamping of di hoofs of im strong ones, at di rushing of im chariots, di rumbling of im wheels, di fathers no look back to dem children, because of di feebleness of hands,
because of di day wey come to destroy all di Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every helper wey remain, because di Lord go destroy di Philistines, di remnant of di coast of Caphtor.
Baldness don come on Gaza. Ashkelon dey cut off, di remnant of dem valley. How long you go cut yourself?”
You sword of di Lord, how long e go be before you dey quiet? Put yourself up into your scabbard. Rest, and dey still.
How e go dey quiet, seeing say di Lord don give am charge? Against Ashkelon, and against di sea shore, na dere e don appoint am.
Concerning Moab. Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “Woe to Nebo! Because e dey laid waste. Kiriathaim dey disgraced, e dey captured. Di high fortress dey disgraced and dismayed.
Di praise of Moab no dey again. For Heshbon dem don devise evil against am: ‘Come, make we cut am off from being nation.’ You also, Madmen, go dey brought to silence. Di sword go pursue you.
Voice of crying from Horonaim, desolation and great destruction!
Moab dey destroyed. Her little ones don cause cry to dey heard.
Because by di ascent of Luhith dem go up with continual weeping, because for di descent of Horonaim dem don hear di distress of cry of destruction.
Flee! Save your lives! Be like juniper for di wilderness.
Because, because you don trust for your works and for your treasures, you go also dey taken. Chemosh go go forth into captivity, im priests and im princes together.
Di destroyer go come on every city, and no city go escape. Di valley also go perish, and di plain go dey destroyed, as di Lord don speak.
Give wings to Moab, so that e go fly away, because im cities go become desolation, without anyone to dwell inside dem.
Cursed be im wey do di work of di Lord negligently. Cursed be im wey keep back im sword from blood.
Moab don dey at ease from im youth, and e don settle on im dregs, and dem no empty am from vessel to vessel, neither e don go into captivity. Therefore im taste remain for am, and im scent no change.
Therefore see, di days dey come,” talk di Lord, “wey I go send to am men wey pour, and dem go pour am out. Dem go empty im vessels, and break im jars in pieces.
Moab go dey ashamed of Chemosh, as di house of Israel dey ashamed of Bethel, dem confidence.
How una go talk, ‘We na mighty men, and valiant men for war’?
Moab dey laid waste, and dem don go up into im cities, and im chosen young men don go down to di slaughter,” talk di King, wey im name na di Lord of Armies.
“Di calamity of Moab dey near to come, and im affliction hurry fast.
All una wey dey round about am, bemoan am. All una wey know im name, talk, ‘How di strong sceptre dey broken, di beautiful staff!’
You daughter wey dwell for Dibon, come down from your glory, and sit for thirst, because di destroyer of Moab don come up against you. E don destroy your strongholds.
Inhabitant of Aroer, stand by di way and watch. Ask am wey flee, and her wey escape. Talk, ‘Wetin don happen?’
Moab dey disgraced, because e dey broken down. Howl and cry. Tell am for Arnon say Moab dey laid waste.
Judgment don come on di plain country, on Holon, and on Jahzah, and on Mephaath,
and on Dibon, and on Nebo, and on Beth Diblathaim,
and on Kiriathaim, and on Beth Gamul, and on Beth Meon,
and on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, and on all di cities of di land of Moab, far or near.
Di horn of Moab dey cut off, and im arm dey broken,” talk di Lord.
“Make am drunk, because e don magnify imself against di Lord. Moab go wallow for im vomit, and e go also dey ridiculed.
Israel no dey ridiculed to you? E dey found among thieves, say whenever you speak of am, you wag your head?
Una wey dwell for Moab, leave di cities, and dwell for di rock. Be like di dove wey make im nest for di sides of di mouth of di pit.
We don hear of di pride of Moab, say e dey very proud, im loftiness, and im pride, and im arrogance, and di haughtiness of im heart.
I know im wrath,” talk di Lord, “but e no dey right. Im boasts don accomplish nothing.
Therefore I go wail for Moab. Yes, I go cry out for all Moab. Dem go mourn for di men of Kir Heres.
More pass di weeping of Jazer I go weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches pass over di sea. Dem reach even to di sea of Jazer. Di destroyer don fall on your summer fruits and on your vintage.
Joy and gladness dey taken away from di fruitful field, and from di land of Moab. I don cause wine to cease from di winepresses. Nobody go tread with shouting. Di shouting go be no shouting.
From di cry of Heshbon even to Elealeh, even to Jahaz, dem don raise dem voice, from Zoar even to Horonaim, to Eglath Shelishiyah, because di waters of Nimrim also go dey desolate.
Moreover I go cause to cease for Moab,” talk di Lord, “im wey offer for di high place, and im wey burn incense to im gods.
Therefore my heart sound for Moab like flutes, and my heart sound like flutes for di men of Kir Heres, because di riches wey e don get don perish.
Because every head dey bald, and every beard clipped. Cuts dey on all di hands, and sackcloth on di loins.
On all di housetops of Moab and for di streets of am, everywhere dey lamentation, because I don break Moab like vessel wey no dey pleasure,” talk di Lord.
“How e dey broken down! How dem howl! How Moab don turn im back with shame! So Moab go become derision and terror to all wey dey round am.”
Because di Lord talk like dis: “See, e go fly like eagle, and go spread out im wings against Moab.
Di cities dey taken, and di strongholds dey seized. Di heart of di mighty men of Moab for dat day go be like di heart of woman for her labour pains.
Moab go dey destroyed from being people, because e don magnify imself against di Lord.
Fear, and di pit, and di snare dey upon you, inhabitant of Moab,” talk di Lord.
“Im wey flee from di fear go fall into di pit, and im wey get up out of di pit go dey caught for di snare, because I go bring on am, even on Moab, di year of dem visitation,” talk di Lord.

“Dem wey flee stand without strength under di shadow of Heshbon, because fire don go out of Heshbon, and flame from di middle of Sihon, and e don devour di corner of Moab, and di crown of di head of di sons of tumult.
Woe to you, Moab! Di people of Chemosh perish, because dem don take your sons captive, and your daughters into captivity.
Yet I go cause di captivity of Moab to return for di latter days,” talk di Lord. Dis far na di judgment of Moab.
